newsitem.title: UK: Analysts say debt mkt worries over Yeltsin overdone.
newsitem.headline: Analysts say debt mkt worries over Yeltsin overdone.

text.p: Russian debt prices, at record highs in the morning, slumped on news on Thursday that President Boris Yeltsin will have heart surgery but analysts said the worries are overdone and the country's outlook remains positive.
Yeltsin, who had largely disappeared from public view since winning a second term in office in July, said on Thursday he had agreed to undergo a heart operation, probably later this month.
"Everyone assumed this was the state of Yeltsin's health. The government wasn't winning any points by concealing it," said Merrill Lynch analyst Daniel McGovern.

Prices for Vneshekonombank debt -- old Soviet commercial debt which Russia and its creditors are on the verge of restructuring -- tumbled more than three points to 61 percent of face after hitting a record high earlier in the morning.
Russian shares also fell sharply but later recovered some of the lost ground.
"The fact they are doing something about it (Yeltsin's health) is good news rather than bad," UBS analyst Alex Mitcheson-Smith said.
Debt prices have been rising since Yeltsin's election victory and the installation of his pro-reform government and analysts predict further gains this year.
"We're buying like mad. This was on the cards that he might have an operation...there's a high chance the operation will be successful," said ANZ economist Jerome Booth.
"Even if he does die, I think there's a 90 percent chance there will be no change in basic economic policy," he added.

The analysts said Russia had clear constitutional rules to cover the handover of power should Yeltsin be disabled, with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin taking over for three months until new elections are held.
McGovern said nobody wanted another economically ruinous election and was political leaders weere likely to seek a middle ground if Yeltsin was out of power.
There is investor concern over the role security chief, and early presidential candidate, Alexander Lebed might play in such a scenario, but McGovern doubted he would make a grab for power.
However, sparks might fly if Lebed tried to meddle in economic affairs, he added.
Analysts have all but written off the chances of the Communists taking over the presidency.
"The most likely scenario is positive," said Mitcheson-Smith.
November's expected Russian Eurobond issue should help lift up the prices of other Russian debt, though they were getting close to levels where profit-taking would come in, he said.
"U.S. investors are likely to be worried, seeing the market come off, but really the only issue is to work out how far prices will go and to buy at the appropriate moment," said Booth.
"I would recommend to start buying right now in case it bounces up again. Itt's quite volatile. Buy now, and if it goes lower buy more," he added.
